title: HarborByte Pilot: Cost Playbook + Benchmark Scoping
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot pricing + token econ spreadsheet by 2027-12-08
SE to share benchmark runbook and script links (GDrive) by 2027-12-07
Schedule infra check / VPN/VPC exchange the week of 2027-12-13
Customer to confirm 3 workload samples and SLOs by 2027-12-09
action_items: Carlos Reyes - Prepare 3-run benchmark template and perf metrics sheet (due 2027-12-07)
Maya Patel - Share pricing spreadsheet + example contract language (due 2027-12-08)
Ravi Malhotra - Provide sample payloads and token distribution (due 2027-12-09)
Evelyn Shaw - Confirm stakeholders and success criteria, loop in infra (due 2027-12-09)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week pilot focused on unit economics and benchmark validation. Discussed expected workloads (chat + long context retrieval), target per-token cost, batching + KV/prefix caching knobs, quantization options, and pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: share pricing spreadsheet, benchmark runbook, and sample payloads; schedule benchmark runs and infra handoff.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (latency p95/p99, throughput, cost per 1k tokens)
Batching and caching knobs (max batch, batching window, prefix cache)
transcript: [00:00] Maya Patel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Evelyn Shaw (HarborByte): Evelyn here, Head of Platform. Ravi's on, Lina's here, Tom will pop in around 15 minutes.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Great. Carlos, want to intro yourself?
[00:25] Carlos Reyes (Redwood SE): Hi all, Carlos, SE on inference perf and cost modeling. I'll drive the benchmark plan and help with the scripts.
[00:40] Ravi Malhotra: Quick note — our primary workload is user-facing chat (short prompts, lots of small RTTs) plus a few multi-turn long-context retrieval flows that hit ~8k tokens occasionally.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Perfect. For the pilot, we usually scope 2–3 workload slices. Today let's define success criteria — what would success look like for HarborByte at the end of four weeks?

[01:22] Evelyn Shaw: Two things: (1) show we can hit sub-$0.003 per 1k-token for the bulk chat workload and (2) p95 latency under 200ms for the short prompts on a dedicated setup. Also need security posture check — SOC2 + KMS integration — Lina will handle the compliance side.
[01:45] Lina Ortiz: Yup, we'll need audit logs and key controls. Also, budget constraint: Q1 pilot budget is $12k, so we need an econ playbook that fits that runway.

[02:10] Carlos Reyes: Okay good context. Economically, target of $0.003 per 1k is aggressive but feasible with batching + KV/prefix caching and quantization. We'll show tradeoffs: higher batching improves unit cost but increases tail latency. We'll parameterize batch size, batching window, and cache hit rate in the model.
[02:40] Ravi Malhotra: Our traffic is bursty — median payloads are 60 tokens, but we have bursts where 200 concurrent users hit it. We care about P95 more than average.

[03:05] Maya Patel: Noted. For benchmarking we'll run two modes: Hosted Redwood (fast path) and a Dedicated reserved pool to show both latency and unit-econ differences. Any preference for quant levels? We can do fp16 and 4-bit quant (q4_0/q4_1 equivalent) to show cost deltas.
[03:35] Ravi Malhotra: We want quality parity checks first — can't accept big regression. So include ROUGE/BLEU or a small eval set for hallucination/precision checks.
[03:55] Carlos Reyes: Absolutely. We'll include a small eval harness — automated prompts and scoring. Also include human spot-checking for the long-context flows.
[04:20] [Tom Wu joins: Hey all sorry, late train],
[04:28] Tom Wu (CTO): Quick: budget is fixed but if the econ looks good we can greenlight more capacity. Timeline — can this pilot finish before end of Q1?

[04:40] Maya Patel: We're proposing a 4-week pilot starting after infra handoff. Week 0 is prep (keys, VPC peering), Week 1: baseline runs, Week 2: knobs and quant tests, Week 3: scale runs and validation, Week 4: wrap and recommendations. So yes, finishes well before end of Q1.
[05:10] Lina Ortiz: If the prep takes longer we'll need to adjust. Who owns infra handoff?
[05:18] Carlos Reyes: We'll need a tech contact from HarborByte for VPN/VPC peering and an IAM/KMS contact. We can do hosted first while private setup is provisioned — that reduces delay.
[05:35] Ravi Malhotra: Hosted first is fine. We do have strict data retention rules though — logs can't leave region. We'll need to confirm retention knobs.
[05:50] Carlos Reyes: Noted. We'll include a retention & residency checklist in the security docs. Next, on cost modeling: what's your expected token mix? Short chat vs retrieval length distribution?
[06:10] Ravi Malhotra: About 80% short (median 60 tokens), 15% medium (300 tokens), 5% long (2k–8k tokens). We can send a sample histogram.

[06:30] Maya Patel: Perfect — please send that histogram; it'll drive the unit-econ estimates. We'll show per-token price under different batch sizes: 1 (no batching), 8, 32. Also show impact of cache hit rates at 10%, 40%, 70%.
[06:55] Evelyn Shaw: Can you explain prefix/KV caching in simple terms for finance? We heard 'KV cache' but our infra folks called it something else.

[07:10] Carlos Reyes: Sure. Prefix caching stores partial decoding state for repeated turns — it reduces compute for repeated prompts. KV cache is similar for long contexts (so you don't re-run the whole sequence). On average, a 40% cache hit can cut token compute by ~30% depending on recency patterns.
[07:40] Ravi Malhotra: Are those caches safe for PII? We need controls.
[07:48] Carlos Reyes: Cache is ephemeral and stored encrypted in RAM on the GPU host; for Private we can opt for customer-controlled KMS. We'll document retention and scrub policies.

[08:10] Maya Patel: Moving to bench details — metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, quality metrics (automated scoring), and cache hit rate. SE will share the runbook link.

[08:35] Carlos Reyes: Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/harborbyte-bench-runbook (I'll add access after call). Script will be a small Python harness using our SDK and a container with load generator. We'll provide a YAML config for batch window and max_batch_size.
[09:00] Ravi Malhotra: For load gen, can you simulate our burst pattern? We have diurnal plus sudden spikes from marketing drops.
[09:10] Carlos Reyes: Yes, we can replay traces if you send them; otherwise we'll craft an approximation. The benchmark will run warm, then measure 20-minute steady-state windows plus spike tests.
[09:40] Evelyn Shaw: About unit cost: you mentioned quantization. How much does 4-bit help vs fp16?
[09:48] Carlos Reyes: Ballpark: q4 might reduce GPU cost per token by ~30–40% depending on model size and kernel support. But there can be a small quality delta; we'll include AB tests.
[10:10] Tom Wu: If we go dedicated, what's the commitment? We may want a small reserved pool for predictable throughput.

[10:20] Maya Patel: Dedicated contracts are monthly commits; for pilots we usually do a minimal reserved pool + burst to hosted. We'll show cost curves: fully hosted, hybrid with reserved baseline + hosted burst, and dedicated-only. That will map to your $12k runway.
[10:45] Ravi Malhotra: Can the model be pinned by version? We need deterministic behavior for A/B.
[10:50] Carlos Reyes: Yes, you can pin model versions. We'll also show rollback and canary options in the rollout plan.
[11:10] Evelyn Shaw: For reporting, we need a per-route cost dashboard. Does Redwood console have token-level breakdown per endpoint?
[11:18] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency per route, and you can export CSVs or connect via the API for internal dashboards.
[11:35] Ravi Malhotra: On security docs, Lina — we'll need SOC2 report and sample audit logs. Maya, can you include an example audit log schema?
[11:45] Maya Patel: Yep, I'll add that to the security pack. Action: I'll send SOC2 and sample audit logs with retention options.

[12:10] Carlos Reyes: Back to perf knobs — we'll sweep max_batch_size (1, 8, 16, 32) and batching window (5ms, 20ms, 50ms). We expect batch sizes >8 to improve cost but may push P99 latency up, especially for short prompts.
[12:35] Ravi Malhotra: Sounds right. For our short prompts we want P95 < 200ms and P99 ideally < 350ms. If batching breaks that, we need fallback to single-token low-latency path.
[13:00] Carlos Reyes: Exactly — we can configure per-route latency SLOs with smart routing: if a request must be low-latency, route to a low-batch path or a smaller model variant.
[13:20] Evelyn Shaw: Quality guardrails: if quantized model drifts, we need rollback triggers. Can you add threshold checks?
[13:28] Carlos Reyes: We'll include quality regression alerts tied to the eval set and a canary workflow.

[13:50] Maya Patel: Timeline recap: we aim to start baseline runs week of 2027-12-13. Prep items this week: infra contacts, histogram, signing access to runbook. Then two benchmark weeks and a final recommendation week. Any blockers?
[14:10] Lina Ortiz: We need legal to review pilot MSA — send the standard pilot T&Cs and any data residency clauses.
[14:20] Maya Patel: Will do. I'll add pilot T&Cs to the packet.
[14:40] Ravi Malhotra: On observability, will we get tracing? We need request traces to map token spend per call.
[14:48] Carlos Reyes: Yes, we can enable tracing hooks and provide a tracing export; sample trace format will be in the runbook.

[15:10] [~15:10] Maya Patel: Quick exercise — with your token histogram, we'll produce three costing scenarios: conservative (no caching, minimal batching), expected (medium batching + 40% cache hit), and optimistic (heavy batching + 70% cache). We'll include per-1k-token cost and projected monthly burn at 1M requests.
[15:40] Ravi Malhotra: That would be very helpful. Also include sensitivity to model size — smaller model vs large for the same quality.
[16:00] Carlos Reyes: We'll include a model recommendation matrix (latency vs quality vs cost), and we'll show one candidate small/fast model and one higher-quality model for the retrieval flows.
[16:25] Evelyn Shaw: For acceptance criteria, can we put hard gates? e.g., p95 <= 200ms for short chat, quality delta < 2% on eval, and unit cost <= $0.003/1k in the expected scenario.
[16:40] Maya Patel: Yes — let's capture that as pilot acceptance gates. We'll document them and we'll run the acceptance tests in the final week.
[17:05] Tom Wu: Logistics — who will run the first benchmark? Redwood or HarborByte?

[17:12] Carlos Reyes: We can run an initial baseline on Redwood-hosted to iterate fast; then we'll do a joint run on Dedicated/private with HarborByte infra. For replay fidelity, we may need your trace files.
[17:40] Ravi Malhotra: I'll get those traces over. Expect a CSV with timestamped requests and payload sizes.
[18:05] Maya Patel: Great. Links to be shared: pricing sheet (internal), bench runbook (GDrive), security pack (S3 link). I'll attach in the follow-up email. Any other questions?
[18:25] Lina Ortiz: One more — encryption-at-rest specifics for private deploy?
[18:32] Carlos Reyes: Private allows customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we'll outline options in the security pack.
[19:00] Evelyn Shaw: OK that covers most. Let's confirm the kickoff checklist in the follow-up and lock dates.

[19:10] Maya Patel: Recap of immediate next steps: we send the pricing spreadsheet and security pack by 12/08, SE shares runbook by 12/07, HarborByte provides histograms + traces by 12/09, schedule first benchmark week 12/13. Anything to add?
[19:35] Ravi Malhotra: No, that's good. Thanks everyone.
[19:40] Tom Wu: Thanks — talk soon.
[19:45] Maya Patel: End call. Follow-up email coming with links and ownerships. Bye.
